summary: AVONET (CC BY 4.0, Figshare) gives body mass and linear wing measurements for every extant bird including the ostrich and the heaviest fliers, but not wing area or pectoral muscle mass; PBDB has 108 moa occurrences and 25 species names with no body-size values; MorphoSource has 3 ostrich CT series and no moa. Muscle-power and moa-mass inputs would have to be compiled from the literature (e.g. published moa mass regressions), and comparative sternum/heart datasets on Dryad are skeletal or cardiovascular proxies only.
next_step: Combine AVONET mass and wing length with a compiled table of pectoral-muscle fractions and wing areas (literature) and published moa mass estimates; then pre-register a required-vs-available power comparison across the mass range up to ~70 kg.
obstacles_confirmed: Moa mass and wing reduction are fossil estimates with wide error; PBDB holds no body-size values for Dinornis.
No repository dataset pairs wing area with flight-muscle mass across large birds.
